deep.reconstruction:
Context (from 108v): Riemann is proving what became his paper 'Ueber das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen' (Crelle 65, 1866). Notation: u_k = α_k(z) are the normalized abelian integrals of the first kind. α_k^μ denotes α_k(η_μ) or α_k(ε_μ). The Riemann constant is absorbed into the congruences. Two facts are already established. (A) If θ(u−e) does not vanish identically in z, it has exactly p zeros η_1..η_p, and e ≡ Σ_1^p α(η) holds uniquely. (B) θ(Σ_1^{p−1} α^μ) = 0 for all η_1..η_{p−1}. Hypothesis at the bottom of 108v, as I read it with indices fixed: F_m := θ(u + Σ_1^m(α(η_μ) − α(ε_μ)) − e) vanishes identically in z and all η, ε, but F_{m+1} does not.

Step 1 (top of page). Regard F_{m+1} as a function of z. Setting z = ε_j cancels one pair, giving F_m-type expressions, which vanish identically. So F_{m+1} vanishes at ε_1..ε_{m+1}. By (A) it has p−m−1 further zeros, call them η'_1..η'_{p−m−1}. Fact (A) applied to the shifted argument gives e − Σ_1^{m+1} α(η) + Σ_1^{m+1} α(ε) ≡ Σ_1^{m+1} α(ε) + Σ_1^{p−m−1} α(η'), [mine:] i.e. e ≡ Σ_1^{m+1} α(η_μ) + Σ_1^{p−m−1} α(η'_ν). These points are unique, since otherwise θ would vanish at more than p points without vanishing identically.

Step 2. Regard the same function as a function of one of the η's. Besides the forced zeros, it vanishes at p−m−2 further points ε'. This gives a congruence of the form −e ≡ Σ_1^m α(ε_μ) + Σ_1^{p−m−2} α(ε'), with the ε' uniquely determined.

Step 3 (conclusion). Under the hypothesis, the two congruences
(1) e ≡ Σ_1^p α(η)
(2) −e ≡ Σ_1^{p−2} α(ε)
are solvable with m+1 of the η and m of the ε arbitrary; the rest are then determined. Conversely θ(u−e) ≡ 0 if these hold. Hence: if (1) is solvable in more than one way, then (2) is solvable, and m+1 free η correspond to m free ε (m ≥ 0), and conversely. Modern form: for a degree-p divisor D with h^0(D) = m+1 ≥ 2, the divisor K − D has degree p−2 and h^0(K−D) = m (Riemann–Roch).

Step 4. 'In a quite similar way': if θ(v) = 0, then v ≡ Σ_1^{p−1} α(η) and −v ≡ Σ_1^{p−1} α(ε) are always solvable. Exactly m of the η (and m of the ε) can be chosen freely, the other p−1−m being determined, precisely when θ(Σ_1^m α(η) − Σ_1^m α(ε) + v) vanishes identically but θ(Σ_1^{m+1} α(η) − Σ_1^{m+1} α(ε) + v) does not. This is the Riemann vanishing theorem plus the 'm-fold' refinement: h^0(D_{p−1}) = h^0(K − D_{p−1}) = m+1. This refinement is the germ of the Riemann singularity theorem (mult_v θ = h^0).
errors: Index bookkeeping is loose. The previous page has Σ_0^{m−1}/Σ^{m−1} where the logic of this page (m+1 free η, p−m−1 determined; m free ε, p−m−2 determined) requires F_m ≡ 0 and F_{m+1} ≢ 0. Also the congruence written '(−Σ^{p−2}α + e) ≡ ...' should read −e − Σ(...) ≡ Σ α(ε) (sign/index slip).
Converse ('Offenbar gelten diese Sätze auch umgekehrt') is asserted without proof.

The identification of 'number of freely choosable points' with the order of identical vanishing is stated, not fully proved here. The full equality of theta multiplicity with h^0 was only proved rigorously much later (Kempf 1973).
